_comment: Curated A9 reference data, hand-authored from the 1996 Series II service
manual text layer (§2-173 to §2-185 for the circuit descriptions, §5-2 for
the fault codes, §5-10 and §5-11 for the procedure) and checked page by page
against Figure 7-9 sheets 1-4 and Table 6-10 in both revisions.
There is a curated study document for this board in ../MD/A9_Ohms_Cal.md and
it was mined for circuit narrative, but every number here was re-read from
the PDFs. Two of its statements did not survive that check and are recorded
in the caveats rather than quietly corrected: it calls TP7 RCOM where the
sheet 1 legend prints ACOM, and it concludes that Table 6-10 is wrong about
K23's package where the manual is in fact split two against two.
The fault codes are the whole 3300 block. Twelve name A9 alone (3300-3306,
3308-3310, 3338, 3339). The rest carry an 'A9/A10' title, and they divide
into three groups worth telling apart: those with an explicit A9 verdict
(3311, 3312, 3333, 3334, 3335, 3336), those the manual branches on with a
measurement made on A9 (3313, 3315, 3319, 3325), and those whose verdict is
A10 even though the source and the reading path are A9's. All of them are
kept, because the pattern across the block is what localises a fault: every
one of 3311-3341 is measured through A9's differential amplifier, so a fault
in that amplifier lights the whole range at once and is worth ruling out
before any individual ratio code is believed.

overview.summary: Half of the calibrator's resistance function, and the half that does the thinking. A9 carries only three resistance values of its own -- 1 ohm, 1.9 ohm and a short -- but it holds all of the ohms calibration circuitry except one op amp, the two-wire lead drop compensation circuit, and the 82C55 Programmable Peripheral Interface (U11) whose three ports drive the relay latch/drivers on this board *and* on the Ohms Main assembly (A10). Four blocks make it up. The 2/5/10 V source (K9, Z1, U1, Q1, with Q2 and Q3 switching divider taps) is the current source behind every resistance ratio measurement the instrument makes. The differential amplifier (U2 and U3 in, U4 out, U5 cancelling the current through R18, gain 75 set by resistors in Z1) reads the result and sends it to A11's adc on the RCL line. The two-wire compensation circuit -- a 30 kHz dc-to-dc converter of U6 and T1 making a floating +/-8.2 V supply, chopper amplifier U7 with buffer U8 cancelling the high-side lead drop, and U10 sensing that current to make U9 cancel the low-side drop -- lets a two-wire ohmmeter be calibrated without its own lead resistance spoiling the result. And the digital section (U11, decoders U12 and U13, inverter U22, seven UCN5801 latch/drivers U14-U20 and diagnostic multiplexer U21) switches the board's 31 latching relays and reports the diagnostic lines back on SDL. The 1 ohm value is four 4 ohm wirewounds in parallel in R41; the 1.9 ohm value is two 3.8 ohm wirewounds in parallel in R42; K7 and K8 select the short.
overview.connectors: P311 and P312, DIN 41612 type C, 64-pin right-angle. P311 carries the analog side -- OHMS OUT HI/LO, OHMS SENSE HI/LO, INT SENSE LO, OUT LO, DAC OUT HI/LO, DAC SENSE HI, 10V OUT HI, AMP IN, AMP OUT, ACOM, R COM, SDL and RCL. P312 carries the supplies (+/-17 S and S COM, +5 RLH and RLH COM, +5 LH, LH COM and -5 LH) and the guarded digital bus, and re-exports the 82C55's port lines to A10 as OHM PA0-PA7, OHM PB0-PB3 and OHM PC0-PC5.
overview.note: A9 makes no supply of its own except the floating +/-8A pair for the compensation amplifiers. Everything else arrives on P312 from A17 and A19: +/-17 S with S COM for the analog circuits, +5 RLH with RLH COM for the relay drivers, and +5 LH / -5 LH with LH COM for the logic. Those are three different commons and only S COM has a test point (TP12); a meter left on TP12 reads the relay-driver and logic rails wrong. §4-14 also applies here in its strong form: A9 mounts component side to the REAR, so it needs the analog reverse extender card, and §5-10 step 1 has you take the rear shield off before probing.

SOURCE.note: The buffered 13 V reference from A11 arrives through K9 (BRF13 / BSRF13) onto a divider made of resistors in Z1. For 10 V, PB4 and PB5 turn Q2 and Q3 off and the divider is Z1's 15 kohm and 50 kohm sections; for 2 V both FETs are on, paralleling Z1's 11.535 kohm and 3.846 kohm sections with the 50 kohm, which keeps the dissipation in the resistors down at the lower output. The tap is TP11, buffered by U1 (OP-07) with TIP120 Darlington Q1 as the pass element, and leaves as 10V OUT HI at TP13. R11 (330 ohm, 1 W) is Q1's load and R12 (100 kohm) its bleed. CR7 and CR8 clamp the 10V SENSE LO return.

AMP.rails: RCL (differential amplifier output to A11's adc)
AMP.note: Gain 75, set by resistors in Z1. The voltage being measured goes to U3 (+input, TP20); DAC OUT HI and DAC SENSE HI, tied together, go through K12 to U2 (-input, TP19). Both outputs meet at U4 through Z1's gain-setting resistors. The amplifier generates a current through Z1's 1 kohm (pins 1-2) and 75 kohm (pins 2-3) to R COM, and U5, an inverting amplifier clamped by VR3, generates an equal and opposite current through 76 kohm R18 to cancel it. U4's output leaves through R46 and K10 as RCL. Offsets differ per input condition, so the software first switches K11 to reset to tie both inputs together and reads the offset, then adjusts the DAC until the reading returns to it. Above 1 Mohm, U3 makes too much current noise and A10's low-bias FET op amp U1 is switched in ahead of it -- that is what arrives at TP14 as AMP OUT.

COMP.note: A dc-to-dc converter of switching-regulator IC U6 (LT3526) and transformer T1, switching +17 S through T1's primary at about 30 kHz set by R27 and C21. Control line PB7 turns Q6 on, which turns Q5 on, which supplies +17 S to U6 -- so with two-wire comp off the whole circuit is dead by design. Switching spikes on the +17 S line are filtered by L2, R25, C18, C19, C20 and C52. The secondary is rectified by CR1, CR2, CR9 and CR10 into C22 and C23, regulated by 8.2 V zeners VR1 and VR2, and filtered again by R43/L3/C24 and R44/L4/C25 into the +/-8A rails at TP8 and TP9, whose common is ACOM at TP7. C53 and C54 between A COM and S COM keep switching noise off the calibration resistor. High-side cancellation: the ohmmeter's current enters at A COM, leaves U8 through Z2's 500 ohm and K29 to the calibration resistor, and U7 -- a chopper-stabilised LTC1052 protected by CR3-CR6 and R45 -- holds its own input difference at zero so the path drop goes to zero. Low-side cancellation: U10 (OP215) senses the current across Z2's 500 ohm and, with Z2's four 10 kohm resistors, drives U9 to push an equal and opposite current through Z2's 1 kohm and K28A into OHMS SENSE LO.

OHMS.rails: OHMS OUT HI/LO, OHMS SENSE HI/LO, OUT LO, INT SENSE LO
OHMS.note: The 1 ohm value is four 4 ohm wirewound resistors in parallel inside R41, the 1.9 ohm value two 3.8 ohm wirewounds in parallel inside R42, and both are supplied as matched sets specified at 0.04 % and 3 ppm/degC. K4 and K5 connect them to OHMS OUT HI and OHMS SENSE HI; K6 and K30 to OHMS OUT LO and OHMS SENSE LO; K7 and K8 select the short. Although they live here they operate as part of the Ohms Main assembly, filling out the bottom of the range. A9 also carries the relays that switch the low side of whichever resistance is selected onto the output bus -- the high sides are switched on A10 -- with K24 connecting OHMS OUT LO to OUT LO and K25 connecting OHMS SENSE LO to INT SENSE LO.

faultCodes.title: A9: 8255 Control Word
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics read back the control word of the 82C55 (U11).
faultCodes.expected: The control word reads back as written
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is probably at fault. Nothing else in the 3300 block can be trusted while this fails, and neither can A10: U11's three ports drive the latch/drivers on both boards, so every other ohms measurement is being made through hardware that is not known to be listening.

faultCodes.title: A9: 8255 Port a Fault
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics write data to port A of U11 and read it back.
faultCodes.expected: Data written to port A reads back
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is probably at fault. Port A is the common input bus to U14-U20 and to multiplexer U21, and it is routed on to A10's relay drivers as well, so with this failing no relay on either ohms board can be set.

faultCodes.title: A9: 8255 Port B Fault
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics read port B of U11 during the instrument's dormant state.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is probably at fault. PB0-PB3 feed decoder U12 (PB3 inverted by U22) and go on to A10; PB4, PB5 and PB6 are the gates of Q2, Q3 and Q4; PB7 is what turns the two-wire compensation supply on through Q6 and Q5. A stuck bit here can therefore present as a source that will not change range, or as a dead +/-8A rail.

faultCodes.title: A9: 8255 Port C Fault
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics read port C of U11 during the instrument's dormant state.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is probably at fault. PC0-PC3 drive decoder U13, which enables the latch/drivers two at a time (three on its OUT7); PC4 goes to A10 to strobe its non-latching relay drivers; PC6 enables the diagnostic multiplexer U21. PC7 is unused.

faultCodes.title: A9: 10V Source Fault
faultCodes.measure: The 2/5/10 V source is set for 10 V and routed to A11's adc on the SDL line. Verify with a DMM, hi to TP13 and low to TP12.
faultCodes.verdict: Out of tolerance at TP13 means the 2/5/10 V source circuit on A9 is faulty. In tolerance at TP13 means the source is fine and the diagnostic circuit on A9 -- multiplexer U21 and the Z3/Z4 dividers that feed it -- is probably at fault instead. A note printed against this code and the next two adds: if extender cards are available, verify that 10V SENSE LO is tied to SCOM, a connection made by relays on both ohms assemblies.

faultCodes.title: A9: 5V Source Fault
faultCodes.measure: The 2/5/10 V source is set for 5 V and routed to A11's adc on the SDL line.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the 2/5/10 V source circuit on A9 is probably at fault. The code names no test point of its own; measure at TP13 to TP12 as for 3304. Same extender-card note about 10V SENSE LO.

faultCodes.title: A9: 2V Source Fault
faultCodes.measure: The 2/5/10 V source is set for 2 V and routed to A11's adc on the SDL line.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the 2/5/10 V source circuit on A9 is probably at fault. 2 V is the setting that needs Q2 and Q3 both on to parallel Z1's 11.535 kohm and 3.846 kohm sections with its 50 kohm, so a 2 V failure with 10 V and 5 V passing points at those FETs or at PB4/PB5.

faultCodes.title: A9: Diff Amp Offset Fault
faultCodes.measure: The DAC output is set to 0 V and connected to both inputs of the differential amplifier; the output goes to A11's adc on the RCL line and ten readings are taken.
faultCodes.expected: Spread (highest minus lowest) not more than 1 mV, and absolute value not more than 10 mV
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the differential amplifier circuit on A9 is probably at fault. Check this before believing any of 3311-3341: every one of them is read through this amplifier.

faultCodes.title: A9: Diff Amp Gain Fault
faultCodes.measure: The DAC output is set to 86.7 mV into the -input with the +input at R COM; the output is compared against the 6.5 V reference through A11's adc on RCL.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the differential amplifier circuit on A9 is probably at fault. The gain is set entirely by resistors inside Z1, so a gain error that is not an op amp is Z1.

faultCodes.title: A9: Diff Amp Noise Fault
faultCodes.measure: As 3308 -- DAC at 0 V into both inputs, ten readings through A11's adc on RCL.
faultCodes.expected: Spread (highest minus lowest) not more than 1 mV
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the differential amplifier circuit on A9 is probably at fault. 3310 is 3308 without the absolute-value half of the test, so 3308 and 3310 together failing means noise; 3308 alone means offset.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: Ohms 10:1 Divider Fault
faultCodes.measure: The 2/5/10 V source is set to 10 V across the 100 kohm resistance in Z5, reading the resulting voltage across its 10 kohm portion.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is probably at fault -- Z5 is on this board. This and 3312 are the two codes that test A9's own reference divider, so they are the ones to trust when everything downstream also fails.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: Ohms 1:1 Divider Fault
faultCodes.measure: The 2/5/10 V source is set to 10 V across the 100 kohm resistance in Z5 and the whole arrangement is measured.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is probably at fault. Failing 3312 while 3311 passes points at the measurement path rather than the divider ratio.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 10 Kilohm Diagnostic Fault
faultCodes.measure: The source is set to 10 V across 20 kohm -- Z5's 10 kohm in series with A10's 10 kohm string -- and the drop across A10's string is read. Measure it with a DMM hi to TP2 and low to TP1 on A9.
faultCodes.verdict: Branched, and the branch is on sign as well as magnitude: greater than 5 V blames the Ohms Main assembly (A10), less than or equal to 5 V blames the Ohms Cal assembly (A9). Note the polarity the manual asks for -- hi on TP2 (OHMS OUT LO) and low on TP1 (OHMS OUT HI).

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 19 Kilohm Cal Diag Fault
faultCodes.measure: The source is set to 10 V across 29 kohm -- Z5's 10 kohm in series with A10's 19 kohm string -- and the drop across A10's string is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 10 Ohm Cal Diag Fault
faultCodes.measure: The source is set to 2 V across A10's 100 ohm string and the 0.2 V across its 10 ohm portion goes to the diff amp -input; the DAC is set to 2 V across Z5's 100 kohm and the 0.2 V across its 10 kohm portion goes to the +input. The difference is read on RCL. Verify the divided DAC voltage of 0.2 V ±5 % at the +input with a DMM hi to TP20 and low to TP10.
faultCodes.expected: 0 V ±3 % ±15 mV at the amplifier output; 0.2 V ±5 % at TP20
faultCodes.verdict: If the voltage at TP20 is out of tolerance the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is probably at fault. This is the check that separates Z5's divider from the rest of the 10 ohm calibration diagnostic.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 19 Ohm Cal Diag Fault
faultCodes.measure: As 3315 but across A10's 190 ohm string.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the calibration of the 19 ohm resistance on the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 100 Kilohm Ratio Fault
faultCodes.measure: The 2/5/10 V source is set to 10 V, routed to A10 and connected to the 100 kohm string; the drop across its 10 kohm portion is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault. The source and the reading path are A9's, so rule out 3304-3310 first.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 190 Kilohm Ratio Fault
faultCodes.measure: 10 V from the source across A10's 190 kohm string; the drop across its 19 kohm portion is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 1M Ohm Ratio Fault
faultCodes.measure: 10 V from the source across A10's 1 Mohm string; the drop across its 100 kohm portion is read. Measure it with a DMM hi to TP14 and low to TP2 on A9.
faultCodes.verdict: Branched: out of tolerance at TP14 blames the Ohms Main assembly (A10); in tolerance blames the Ohms Cal assembly (A9). 1 Mohm is the first range on which A10's own U1 is switched in ahead of A9's U3, which is why this is the ratio code that names an A9 test point.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 1.9M Ohm Ratio Fault
faultCodes.measure: 10 V from the source across A10's 1.9 Mohm string; the drop across its 190 kohm portion is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 10M Ohm Ratio Fault
faultCodes.measure: 10 V from the source across A10's 10 Mohm string; the drop across its 1 Mohm portion is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 19M Ohm Ratio 1
faultCodes.measure: 10 V from the source across A10's 19 Mohm string; the drop across its 1.9 Mohm portion is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 19M Ohm Ratio 2
faultCodes.measure: 10 V from the source across A10's 19 Mohm string, measured across the whole 19 Mohm.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault. 3322 and 3323 are the two halves of the same ratio: 3322 checks the tap, 3323 the total.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 100M Ohm Ratio Fault
faultCodes.measure: The manual prints this test identically to 3321 -- 10 V from the source connected to the 10 Mohm string, reading the drop across its 1 Mohm portion. For a 100 Mohm ratio it should read the 100 Mohm string and its 10 Mohm portion; see the caveat.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 10 Kilohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: The Current assembly (A7) sources 0.13 mA through INT OUT HI into A10's 10 kohm string. Measure the drop with a DMM hi to TP5 and low to TP6 on A9.
faultCodes.verdict: Branched: out of tolerance at TP5 blames the Ohms Main assembly, in tolerance blames the Ohms Cal assembly. The 33xx check codes differ from the ratio codes in that the current comes from A7 rather than from A9's source, so a whole block of them failing implicates A7 before either ohms board.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 19 Kilohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 0.13 mA into A10's 19 kohm string.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 1 Kilohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 1.3 mA into A10's 1 kohm string.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 1.9 Kilohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 1.3 mA into A10's 1.9 kohm string.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 100 Ohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 13 mA into A10's 100 ohm string.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 190 Ohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 13 mA into A10's 190 ohm string.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 10 Ohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 130 mA into A10's 10 ohm resistance.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 19 Ohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 130 mA into A10's 19 ohm resistance.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 1 Ohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 130 mA through A10 and INT OUT HI into A9's 1 ohm resistance (R41) and the drop across it is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is at fault -- the 1 ohm value is R41 on this board. This is the software version of the first half of §5-10 step 2, and the same relays are implicated: K4, K5 and K6.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 1.9 Ohm Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 13 mA through A10 and INT OUT HI into A9's 1.9 ohm resistance (R42) and the drop across it is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is at fault. Note the band: on a nominal of 24.7 mV the ±15 mV floor dominates, so this code passes anything from about 9 mV to about 40 mV. It catches an open or a shorted path, not a calibration error. The relays are K4, K5 and K30.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: Ohms Short Check Fault
faultCodes.measure: A7 sources 130 mA through A10 and INT OUT HI into A9's short and the drop across it is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is at fault. The short is selected by K7 and K8, and 130 mA through a relay contact makes a millivolt-scale drop visible, so this is really a contact-resistance test on those two relays.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 2 Wire Compensation Fault
faultCodes.measure: The two-wire compensation circuit is driven at its limits with four current-and-load combinations: 10 mA into 10 ohm, -10 mA into 10 ohm, 10 uA into 10 kohm and 5.6 uA into 19 kohm. A7 generates the current, which is routed through A10 and INT OUT HI to A9's A COM; the compensation circuit generates a voltage read on A11's adc via SDL.
faultCodes.verdict: Failure of any of the four tests indicates the two-wire lead drop compensation circuit on A9 is probably at fault. This is the only diagnostic that exercises U7, U8, U9, U10 and the floating supply, so it is the software counterpart of the whole of §5-11. Note that two-wire compensation works only with ohmmeters that source continuous (not pulsed) dc current -- a 'failure' seen at the bench with a pulsed-source meter is not a fault.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: Ohms Correction Factor Fault
faultCodes.measure: The 13 V reference on the DAC assembly is checked by the adc circuit on the DAC assembly.
faultCodes.expected: The 13 V reference within its band
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the DAC assembly (A11) is probably at fault -- nothing on A9 or A10 is measured by this code, despite the A9/A10 title. Since A9's whole 2/5/10 V source is derived from that reference through K9, an A11 reference fault will also fail 3304-3306.

faultCodes.title: Assembly A9 Not Responding
faultCodes.measure: At power up the instrument checks which assemblies are installed; this test verifies whether the Ohms Cal assembly responds.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is probably at fault -- or is simply not seated. This is the give-away code when an ohms fault appears to span both boards: A9's 82C55 controls A10 as well, so a dead A9 presents as everything ohms being wrong with no A10-specific code.

faultCodes.title: A9: 8255 Was Reset
faultCodes.measure: The control word of the 82C55 on the Ohms Cal assembly is read.
faultCodes.expected: The control word still holds what was written to it
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the Ohms Cal assembly (A9) is probably at fault. Distinct from 3300 in what it implies: the part answered once and then lost its configuration, which points at the RESET line (U11 pin 35, driven from POP through R33) or at the +5 LH supply rather than at the device.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 100 Ohm Cal Diag Fault
faultCodes.measure: The source is set to 2 V across A10's 1 kohm string and the 0.2 V across its 100 ohm portion goes to the diff amp -input; the DAC's divided 0.2 V from Z5 goes to the +input. The difference is read on RCL.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the calibration of the 100 ohm resistance on the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault. TP20 to TP10 is still worth measuring first, as in 3315, to clear A9's side of the comparison.

faultCodes.title: A9/A10: 190 Ohm Cal Diag Fault
faultCodes.measure: As 3340 but across A10's 1.9 kohm string, reading the 0.2 V across its 190 ohm portion.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the calibration of the 190 ohm resistance on the Ohms Main assembly (A10) is probably at fault.

componentNotes.U1: OP-07. Buffers the Z1 divider tap (TP11) and drives Darlington pass transistor Q1 to make the 2/5/10 V source output at TP13. One of the three OP-07s in the U1-U3 row of Table 6-10, and the only one of the three that is not part of the differential amplifier.
componentNotes.U2: OP-07, the differential amplifier's inverting input stage. Fed through K12 from DAC OUT HI and DAC SENSE HI tied together, or through K2 from OHMS SENSE HI. Its input is TP19.
componentNotes.U3: OP-07, the differential amplifier's non-inverting input stage; its input is TP20. Above 1 Mohm it makes too much current noise for the job, so §2-184 has A10's low-bias FET op amp U1 switched in ahead of it and the signal arrives on AMP OUT at TP14 instead.
componentNotes.U4: LT1007, the differential amplifier's output stage. Its output goes through R46 to TP15 and then through K10 to the RCL line and A11's adc. Nominal gain of the whole amplifier is 75, set by resistors in Z1.
componentNotes.U5: LM741 inverting amplifier, clamped by 3.3 V zener VR3. The amplifier generates a current through Z1's 1 kohm and 75 kohm sections to R COM, and U5's job is to generate an equal and opposite one through 76 kohm R18 to cancel it.
componentNotes.U6: LT3526 regulating pulse-width modulator, the heart of the two-wire compensation dc-to-dc converter. Switches +17 S through the T1 primary at about 30 kHz set by R27 and C21. It is powered only when PB7 turns Q6 and Q5 on, so a board with two-wire comp off has a dead U6 by design. §5-11 step 1 scopes pin 16 with the common on pin 13.
componentNotes.U7: LTC1052 chopper-stabilised op amp -- the high-side lead drop canceller. It holds the difference between its own pins 4 and 5 at zero, which forces the voltage drop in the path between the ohmmeter and the calibration resistor to zero. Protected by CR3-CR6 and R45. §5-11 step 2 measures its input difference directly and wants less than 4 uV.
componentNotes.U8: NE5534, the buffer that supplies up to 10 mA to the high side. Its output leaves through the 500 ohm in Z2 and K29 to the calibration resistor via OHMS OUT HI.
componentNotes.U9: NE5534, the low-side canceller's output stage. Driven by U10, it pushes a current equal and opposite to the high-side current through Z2's 1 kohm and K28A into OHMS SENSE LO.
componentNotes.U10: OP215 dual JFET-input op amp. Its two non-inverting inputs sit across the 500 ohm in Z2, so with Z2's four 10 kohm resistors it senses the high-side current and tells U9 what to cancel.
componentNotes.U11: CP82C55A Programmable Peripheral Interface -- the digital heart of both ohms assemblies. 24 outputs across three ports: PA0-PA7 the common data bus to the latch/drivers and to U21; PB0-PB3 to decoder U12 (PB3 inverted by U22); PB4/PB5/PB6 the gates of Q2, Q3 and Q4; PB7 through R31 to Q6, which switches the two-wire comp supply on; PC0-PC3 to decoder U13; PC4 to A10's non-latching relay strobe; PC6 the enable for multiplexer U21; PC7 unused. All three ports are also routed to A10 on P312.
componentNotes.U12: MC14028B BCD-to-decimal decoder. Generates the individual latch strobes -- sheet 4 labels its outputs U14 STB, U16 STB, U17 STB, U19 STB and so on, one per driver -- from PB0-PB3 with PB3 inverted by U22.
componentNotes.U13: MC74HC138 3-to-8 line decoder with enable, wired A/B/C to PC0/PC1/PC2 with PC3 driving both enables. Only three outputs are used: OUT5 enables U15 and U16, OUT6 enables U18 and U20, OUT7 enables U14, U17 and U19. §2-174's 'two at a time' is true of two groups out of three, not of all of them -- a line pulling three chips is correct here.
componentNotes.U14: UCN5801A 8-channel high-voltage driver with latch. Enabled by U13 OUT7 together with U17 and U19; decoupled by C45 between +5 RLH and RLH COM.
componentNotes.U15: UCN5801A latch/driver, enabled by U13 OUT5 with U16; decoupled by C41.
componentNotes.U16: UCN5801A latch/driver, enabled by U13 OUT5 with U15; decoupled by C43. Drives the K30, K21, K23 and K20 coils.
componentNotes.U17: UCN5801A latch/driver, enabled by U13 OUT7 with U14 and U19; decoupled by C39.
componentNotes.U18: UCN5801A latch/driver, enabled by U13 OUT6 with U20; decoupled by C42.
componentNotes.U19: UCN5801A latch/driver, enabled by U13 OUT7 with U14 and U17; decoupled by C40.
componentNotes.U20: UCN5801A latch/driver, enabled by U13 OUT6 with U18; decoupled by C41.
componentNotes.U21: MM74HC4051 8-to-1 analog multiplexer, the diagnostic circuit. Five voltage dividers made from resistors in Z3 and Z4 feed it; two of the divider inputs are connected, 10V OUT HI from the source circuit and 2W COMP from the compensation circuit. Its output goes to the SDL line and A11's adc. PC6 enables it.
componentNotes.U22: MC74HCU04 unbuffered hex inverter. Only one section is used in circuit -- it inverts PB3 for U12; sheet 4 shows the other five as N/C.
componentNotes.Q1: TIP120 Darlington, the 2/5/10 V source pass element, with R11 (330 ohm, 1 W) as its load. Table 6-10's 1996 row truncates the package to 'TO-22'; the Rev 9 row and the schematic both say TO-220.
componentNotes.Q2: VN10K VMOS switch on PB4. With Q3 it parallels Z1's 11.535 kohm and 3.846 kohm sections with the 50 kohm to take the source from 10 V down to 2 V, which keeps the dissipation in the divider resistors down.
componentNotes.Q3: VN10K VMOS switch on PB5, working with Q2 on the source divider.
componentNotes.Q4: VN10K VMOS switch on PB6, on the OHMS SENSE LO line on sheet 2.
componentNotes.Q5: 2N3906 PNP. Supplies +17 S to U6 when turned on by Q6, which is what makes the two-wire compensation supply live.
componentNotes.Q6: 2N3904 NPN, driven from PB7 through R31; it turns Q5 on.
componentNotes.T1: The two-wire compensation transformer, Fluke 802652. Its primary is switched by U6 at about 30 kHz; the secondary is rectified by CR1, CR2, CR9 and CR10 into C22 and C23 to make the floating +/-8A pair.
componentNotes.VR1: 8.2 V zener (1N756A) regulating the +8A floating rail at TP8.
componentNotes.VR2: 8.2 V zener (1N756A) regulating the -8A floating rail at TP9.
componentNotes.VR3: 3.3 V zener (1N746A) clamping U5 in the differential amplifier's current-cancellation path.
componentNotes.Z1: Cermet SIP resistor network, Fluke 813659, described in the 1996 list as '5700 LO V INST AMP'. It does two jobs: the 15 kohm / 50 kohm / 11.535 kohm / 3.846 kohm divider that sets the 2/5/10 V source, and the gain-setting resistors (1 kohm at pins 1-2, 75 kohm at pins 2-3, and the input pairs) that make the differential amplifier's gain 75. Marked ESD-sensitive in both parts lists.
componentNotes.Z2: Cermet SIP resistor network, Fluke 809368, '5700 LO V AMP GAIN'. The two-wire compensation circuit's precision elements: a 500 ohm through which U8 sources the ohmmeter's current, four 10 kohm sections that let U10 sense that current, and a 1 kohm through which U9 returns an equal and opposite current. TP18 and TP17 span the 500 ohm; TP16 and TP6 span the 1 kohm.
componentNotes.Z3: Cermet SIP, 10 pin, five 10 kohm elements at ±2 %. With Z4 it forms the five dividers that feed diagnostic multiplexer U21.
componentNotes.Z4: Cermet SIP, 6 pin, five 1 kohm elements at ±2 %. Works with Z3 on the U21 diagnostic dividers.
componentNotes.Z5: Hermetically sealed metal-film SIP divider, Fluke 915889, called 'RNET,MF,HERM,SIP,5700 LO V DIVIDER' in 1996 and 'OHMS CAL REF DIVIDER' in Rev 9. It is the instrument's internal resistance standard: a 100 kohm / 10 kohm pair that the external 10 kohm standard is compared against, and a 90 kohm / 10 kohm 10:1 divider used to calibrate the low ohms values. Fault codes 3311 to 3316, 3340 and 3341 all measure through it. Unlike Z1 and Z2 it carries no ESD asterisk in either parts list, but it is the most accuracy-critical passive part on the board.
componentNotes.R41: Matched resistor set, 1.0 ohm at 0.04 % and 3 ppm/degC, Fluke 824193. Four 4 ohm wirewound resistors in parallel (§2-175); §5-10 step 2 tells you to check all four if the 1 ohm value is wrong.
componentNotes.R42: Matched resistor set, 1.9 ohm at 0.04 % and 3 ppm/degC, Fluke 824201. Two 3.8 ohm wirewound resistors in parallel.
componentNotes.R11: 330 ohm 1 W, Q1's load in the 2/5/10 V source. One of only two 1 W parts on the board, and one of the three rows where the two parts lists genuinely disagree -- see the caveat.
componentNotes.R25: 150 ohm 1 W, in the +17 S feed to U6 with L2, C18, C19, C20 and C52, keeping the converter's switching spikes off the +17 S line. The other of the two 1 W parts, and the other disagreeing row.
componentNotes.R27: 10 kohm metal film, ±1 %, 100 ppm. With C21 (2700 pF) it sets U6's switching rate at about 30 kHz.
componentNotes.R18: 76 kohm metal film at ±0.1 % and 50 ppm -- the tightest single resistor on the board. It carries the cancelling current U5 generates against the differential amplifier's own output current.
componentNotes.R45: 1 kohm, in series with U7's input as protection, working with CR3-CR6 (§2-178).
componentNotes.M4: The Ohms Cal shield, Fluke 775312. §5-10 step 1 tells you to remove the rear shield before putting the board on the extender.
componentNotes.MP4: Fluke 761197. Both parts lists describe it as 'SHIELD, HIGH VOLTAGE CONTROL', which is A14's shield name -- see the caveat. It is a shield on A9's bill of materials whichever name is right.
componentNotes.L2: 6-turn choke in the +17 S feed to the two-wire compensation converter.
componentNotes.L3: 6-turn choke filtering the +8A rail with R43 and C24.
componentNotes.L4: 6-turn choke filtering the -8A rail with R44 and C25.
componentNotes.L5: 6-turn choke on the +5 RLH relay-driver supply, decoupled by C33.
componentNotes.L6: 6-turn choke on the +5 LH logic supply, decoupled by C36.
componentNotes.L7: 6-turn choke on the +17 S analog supply as it enters on P312.
componentNotes.L8: 6-turn choke on the -17 S analog supply as it enters on P312.

caveats.title: K23's relay package: the manual is split two against two
caveats.text: Four places in the manual say what kind of relay K23 is, and they do not agree. Table 6-10 puts it in the 'RELAY,ARMATURE,2 FORM C,5V,LATCH' row (Fluke 769307), in both the 1996 and the Rev 9 revisions, and both give that row a Tot Qty of 20 which matches its 20 designators exactly. Figure 7-9 sheet 1 draws K23's contacts in a block labelled 2FCL, agreeing with the parts list. But the bottom-view key on that same sheet lists K23 among '4FCL BOTTOM VIEW: K6-K9, K12, K14, K19, K21, K23, K28-K30' and leaves it out of the 2FCL list, and Figure 7-9 sheet 4 labels K23's coil -- in U16's group, beside K30, K21 and K20 -- as 4FCL. All four sources agree there are 31 relays; they disagree about which side of the 20/11 split K23 falls on. This dataset carries the parts list's answer, because the parts list is what you order from and because the contact symbol on sheet 1 agrees with it, but the disagreement is real and unresolved: count the pins before ordering. A 2 form C part has 10 and a 4 form C part has 16, so the board settles it in a glance. The curated study document in ../MD/ reports only two of these four sources and concludes the parts list is wrong; that conclusion is not supported once the sheet 1 contact symbol is read.

caveats.title: R14 and R15: 24 ohm in both parts lists, 30 ohm on the schematic
caveats.text: Table 6-10 lists R14 and R15 as 'RES,CF,24,+-5%,0.25W' (Fluke 817528) in both revisions of the manual. Figure 7-9 sheet 2 prints both as 30. They are the series resistors between the +17 S / -17 S rails and the local +17 / -17 nodes that feed the source and differential amplifier blocks, with C7/C8 and C9/C10 after them, so the difference matters for how much the rails sag under load but not for whether the circuit works. The parts list is the authority for what to order; the value carried in this dataset is therefore 24 ohm, and the schematic's 30 is recorded here rather than being reconciled away.

caveats.title: TP7 is ACOM, not RCOM
caveats.text: The TEST POINT INFORMATION box at zone D1 of Figure 7-9 sheet 1 prints 'TP7 = ACOM (PG3 C3)', and sheet 3 labels the node beside the TP7 flag ACOM. That is the floating common of the two-wire compensation supply -- the point at which the ohmmeter's own current enters the board, and the reference for U7 and U8 -- and it is deliberately not tied to S COM. The curated study document in ../MD/A9_Ohms_Cal.md calls TP7 RCOM in two places. R COM is a different net on this board (P311 pins 23A/23C, brought to S COM through K27 at TP10), so substituting one for the other while making the §5-11 step 1 measurement gives a plausible-looking reading of a supply that is not the one being tested.

caveats.title: The procedure is two printed sections walked as one sequence
caveats.text: Chapter 5 prints A9's troubleshooting as §5-10 (two steps) and §5-11, Two-wire Compensation Circuit (two steps), both starting on page 5-56 and each numbered from 1. They are walked here as one sequence, so §5-10 step 1 becomes the prerequisite paragraph and the three numbered steps below are §5-10 step 2, §5-11 step 1 and §5-11 step 2. Every step names its own section. Unlike A14 -- where §5-19 step 6's forward reference to 'step 10' proved the two sections had once been numbered continuously -- the manual gives no cross-reference here that requires the merge: §5-11 step 1 ends 'if these supply voltages are correct skip to step 2', and that resolves inside §5-11, which is to say to step 4 of this combined sequence and not to step 2 of it. The renumbering is this dataset's, not the manual's, and step 2 of this sequence is the 1 ohm / 1.9 ohm / short check rather than the place §5-11 is sending you.

caveats.title: Step 3's text is missing a sentence, and the sentence named four suspects
caveats.text: Step 3 used to read '...verify it displays a waveform similar the associated components. If this signal is correct then check T1, CR1, CR2, CR9, CR10, VR1, VR2...' -- a sentence had gone. The manual prints '...verify it displays a waveform similar the / Figure 5-16. If a failure is detected, check U6, Q5, Q6, Control line PB7, and / associated components.' The middle line is a wrapped continuation that happens to begin with 'Figure 5-16.', and the shared procedure parser dropped any line matching that shape as a stray figure caption, taking the sentence it was continuing with it. So the branch for a BAD waveform went missing while the branch for a GOOD one survived, and nothing about the result looked damaged -- which is what made it worth recording. That has been fixed in tools/build_data.py: a line of that shape is now kept when the line above it has stopped mid-phrase, which is what separates a wrapped reference from a real caption. Step 3 is complete above and Q5 and Q6 are linked again. The mitigations are kept as well -- TP8 and TP9 both list U6, Q5 and Q6 in what to check, TP8's note explains PB7's part, and the U6 pin 16 probe point spells out both branches in full. Still true and not fixed: step 2 prints '8505A IN LO to TP 2' with a space, so TP2 is not linked from that step although TP1, TP5 and TP6 are.

caveats.title: Step references are picked out of prose one token at a time
caveats.text: The designators highlighted on a procedure step are extracted token by token, so a range or a shared prefix in the printed sentence links only what is written out in full. On this board that is visible in step 2, where 'check relays K4, K5, K6, and the four wire-wound resistors in R41' links all four correctly, but any step that wrote a range would link only its endpoints. Read the sentence, not just the chips it lit up.

caveats.title: MP4 is described as A14's shield
caveats.text: Table 6-10 gives MP4 as 'SHIELD, HIGH VOLTAGE CONTROL', Fluke 761197, in both revisions -- and High Voltage Control is A14, not A9. M4 on the same table is 'SHIELD, OHMS CAL', Fluke 775312. §5-10 step 1 refers to 'the rear shield' of this assembly in the singular. So A9's bill of materials carries two shields, one of which is named after another board. Nothing here resolves which physical part is which; both are recorded as printed, and the description of MP4 should not be taken as evidence about where the part goes.

caveats.title: Three parts changed between the two revisions
caveats.text: Joining the two parts lists on Fluke stock number leaves exactly three rows that do not join, and all three are genuine revision differences rather than scanning errors. R11 is 'RESISTOR A52R,RES,MOX,330,+-5%,1W,200PPM' stock 689604 in the 1996 list and 'RES,CC,330,+-5%,1W' stock 163394, an Allen-Bradley GB3311, in Rev 9 -- a change from metal oxide to carbon composition, or rather back from it, since Rev 9 is the earlier revision and the one the photographed board matches. R25 is the same story at 150 ohm: 689612 metal oxide against 178566 carbon composition (GB1515). And VR1/VR2 are stock 386771 in 1996, described as 'ZENER 1N756A A52R', against 810309 in Rev 9 with manufacturer part 1N756ARR1 -- the same 8.2 V device under a different Fluke number. Each carries its Rev 9 row as asBuilt. Order against the 1996 numbers.

caveats.title: Two hardware rows disagree on quantity and one on material
caveats.text: The two lists differ on three mechanical rows in ways too small to fail a join but worth knowing. MP3 (SLEEV,PVC,0.500ID,CLEAR, stock 113761) has a Tot Qty of 1 in the 1996 list and 2 in Rev 9. MP6-MP17 (the soluble spacers, stock 296319) is twelve designators with a Tot Qty of 12 in 1996 and 15 in Rev 9 -- the designator range is the same in both, so one of the two quantity cells is simply wrong. And H1-H4 are 'RIVET,S-TUB,OVAL,AL' in 1996 against '...,STL' in Rev 9, aluminium against steel. None of these three appears on the locator drawing.

caveats.title: Figure 5-16's caption and its axis labels both contradict the step
caveats.text: §5-11 step 1 tells you to connect the oscilloscope to pin 16 of U6 with the scope common on pin 13, set to 5 V/div at 10 us/div, and compare against Figure 5-16. The figure is captioned 'Waveform at Pin 13 of U6' -- pin 13 is the common, not the signal -- and its artwork is annotated 1 V and 10 ms, which is neither the vertical nor the horizontal scale the step asks for. Follow the step's text and its scope settings; use the figure for the shape of the waveform only.

caveats.title: Fault code 3324 prints the same test as 3321
caveats.text: 3321 (10M Ohm Ratio Fault) and 3324 (100M Ohm Ratio Fault) are printed with identical text in §5-2: 'the 2/5/10V SOURCE circuit on the Ohms Cal assembly is set to 10V which is routed to the Ohms Main assembly and connected to the 10 MΩ string. The resulting 1V across the 1 MΩ portion is measured for 1V ±3% ±15 mV.' By the pattern every other ratio code follows -- each value against the decade below it -- 3324 should read the 100 Mohm string and the drop across its 10 Mohm portion. The code's own title and the 3317-3324 sequence say the same. This dataset carries the text as printed and flags it here rather than correcting it.

caveats.title: The 1.9 ohm check code's band is dominated by its floor
caveats.text: Fault code 3334 expects 24.7 mV ±3 % ±15 mV. Three per cent of 24.7 mV is 0.74 mV, so the ±15 mV floor is more than twenty times the proportional term and the code passes anything from about 9 mV to about 40 mV. It is a continuity test on K4, K5, K30 and R42, not a calibration test, and a 1.9 ohm value that is several per cent out will pass it. §5-10 step 2's four-terminal measurement at ±0.1 % is the check that would catch that, and it is not run by the diagnostics.

caveats.title: Every relay on this board is latching, and holds state with the power off
caveats.text: All 31 relays are latching armature types, and §5-10 step 1 turns that into the board's main troubleshooting technique: set the calibrator to the failing function, switch it off, and the relays stay where they were, so the path can be traced cold. It also means a board pulled after a fault comes out in the failing configuration and will still be in it when it goes back. Individual relays are checked by putting an external supply -- the manual suggests a 9 V battery -- across the set coil or the reset coil. Sheet 1's bottom-view keys give the pinouts (4FCL: 7,5,3,1,2,4,6,8 over 10,12,14,16,15,13,11,9; 2FCL: 1,2,4,6,8 over 16,15,13,11,9) and sheet 4 shows every coil with its set and reset windings. These are 5 V coils designed for millisecond latching pulses; pulse them briefly.

caveats.title: §2-174's 'two latch/driver ICs at a time' is true of two groups out of three
caveats.text: §2-174 says decoder U13 enables two latch/driver ICs at a time. There are seven drivers on A9, so they cannot pair evenly, and sheet 4 shows what actually happens: U13's OUT5 enables U15 and U16, OUT6 enables U18 and U20, and OUT7 enables three -- U14, U17 and U19. The other five outputs are not connected. An enable line found pulling three chips is correct rather than a short.

caveats.title: The 0.22 uF driver decoupling capacitors read as 22 uF at low resolution
caveats.text: Each UCN5801 has its own decoupling capacitor between +5 RLH and RLH COM at its COM pin -- C39 to C43 and C45, part of the fifteen-position 0.22 uF polyester row in Table 6-10. Sheet 4 prints them as '.22uF', and at the resolution of the scan the leading decimal point is easy to lose. There is no 22 uF part anywhere on A9; the largest capacitor on the board is C36 at 47 uF and the next is C19/C24/C25 at 10 uF.

caveats.title: Three test points share one printed name
caveats.text: TP16, TP17 and TP18 all read '2 WIRE COMP. CIRCUIT' in the sheet 1 legend, so the legend alone cannot tell them apart. §5-11 step 2 is what disambiguates them: TP18 to TP17 spans the 500 ohm resistor in Z2 and TP16 to TP6 spans the 1 kohm. The legend's own zone references separate TP16 (PG3 B3) from TP17 and TP18 (both PG3 B5). The signal names carried in this dataset add that distinction so the three are not interchangeable in search.
